What is the total order when one failure kind contains both field entries and record entries, or records drawn from more than one A06 list?
When one failure kind has both field entries and record entries, which group comes first, and where do nested fields appear relative to their containing record?
Which list supplies the order when records come from several lists, from an uploaded file, or from a collection for which A06 declares no order?

topics.topic: Clarify whether read_import_mapping advances the owner session last-request reading
questions: Is advancing the owner session's last-request reading an observable effect of read_import_mapping, or solely an earlier effect of owner_sessions.admit_owner_request outside this operation, whose Observable effect is stated as None and whose inputs contain no session?

quotes:
At its arrival a request carrying a valid session restarts the session's
30 minutes, whatever its answer — a CSRF refusal included; of concurrent
arrivals the latest counts (A13 rule 2). A sign-out's admission marks the
session signed out at once.
judgement.why: owner_sessions.admit_owner_request advances last_request at arrival before read_import_mapping runs, so the latter remains effect-free and cannot independently advance the session.

topics.topic: Decide whether a pass becoming runnable exactly at a deadline executes or skips that deadline
questions: If the pass becomes runnable exactly at a scheduled deadline, is that deadline executed or skipped in favour of the following deadline?

quotes:
- **Passes.** `instance_lifecycle` makes each of its two passes every
  interval from the start, as A13 rule 2 says of the session pass: the n-th
  call is due when `clock.monotonic_reading` shows n intervals since serving
  began, the first one interval after; a call due while the previous call of
  the same pass is still running is not made, and the pass waits for the
  next due one; deadlines that pass during a suspension of the host or a
  long call are not made up — the next call is the first deadline after
  the pass can run again. The passes run apart, neither waiting for the
  other. A look of the backup pass answers at once: a run it starts goes on
  apart from the pass, so the looks go on every interval while a run goes
  on, and a look during a run starts none (A18 rule 1).
judgement.divergence: One scheduler executes a pass when it becomes runnable exactly on its deadline, while another treats 'after' as strict and waits for the following deadline; the owner or host observes the different time at which a due backup starts and becomes visible.
judgement.why: The text says calls are due on the deadline but also selects the first deadline after the pass becomes runnable, without defining the equality boundary.

witness.initial: Serving began at monotonic reading 0; a backup look at reading 60 saw the date before 03:00 UTC; the host is then suspended and becomes runnable exactly at the reading-120 deadline, now after 03:00, with no run made and no kept backup for the date.
events: The host resumes exactly at monotonic reading 120.
outcomes: The reading-120 deadline is executed, so run_daily_backup_if_due looks and starts the due backup then.
The reading-120 deadline is skipped as not being after the runnable instant, so the next look is at reading 180.
witness.observer: The owner through the newest-kept-backup page, and the host through the backup files.
basis:
In order: `configuration.load_configuration`;
`backups.probe_backup_location`; `store.open_store`; the owner interface's
listener and then, unless the start is owner-only, the service API's, at
the imported `OWNER_INTERFACE_LISTEN_ADDRESS` and
`SERVICE_API_LISTEN_ADDRESS` constants; then the surfaces answer; then two
passes: `owner_sessions.end_expired_sessions` every imported
`SESSION_PASS_SECONDS` and, except in an owner-only start,
`backups.run_daily_backup_if_due` every imported `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS`, each
from the start as Conventions, "Passes", says.

Due at the first look at or after 03:00 UTC, by `clock.recorded_now`, of a
date an earlier look of this process saw before 03:00, when this process
did not run it, no run is going and no kept backup of the date exists; a
run's date remembered, failed included (A18 rule 1); runs never overlap; the
unencrypted copy removed before the check; a kept name never overwritten;
only files under the two prefixes touched (rule 5); step 3 whatever step 2
did, one cutoff, in name order (rule 4).

topics.topic: Define handling of request bodies exceeding their declared length
questions: What happens when the body contains more bytes than its declared length but remains within IMPORT_FILE_MAX_BYTES: must Registry reject the length mismatch, read and parse all received bytes, or stop at the declared length?

quotes:
The limit is counted
over the bytes Registry receives, never over a length the request
declares: a declared length over the limit is refused before any byte is
read; otherwise Registry reads the upload up to one byte more than the
limit and refuses it as soon as it holds more than the limit, whatever
length was declared or whether one was.

After an upload's answer, whatever it was — accepted, or refused before any
or after some bytes were read — `owner_interface` discards the unread
remainder of the body without reading it into anything and closes the
connection its listener accepted; a connection that carried an upload is
never reused.
judgement.why: P3 judged the same declared-length-overrun question on these unchanged passages, and no subsequent change alters that answer.

precedent.topic: Handling of an upload body longer than its declared length
quotes:
The limit is counted
over the bytes Registry receives, never over a length the request
declares: a declared length over the limit is refused before any byte is
read; otherwise Registry reads the upload up to one byte more than the
limit and refuses it as soon as it holds more than the limit, whatever
length was declared or whether one was.

After an upload's answer, whatever it was — accepted, or refused before any
or after some bytes were read — `owner_interface` discards the unread
remainder of the body without reading it into anything and closes the
connection its listener accepted; a connection that carried an upload is
never reused.
precedent.why: The received-byte rule makes the declared length non-authoritative below the size limit, so the operation reads the upload rather than stopping at that length, while the interface discards only a remainder left after the answer.

topics.topic: Define validation constraints for project display names and Customer names
questions: What form, beyond being present and non-blank, applies to a project display name or Customer name, given that A02 declares no name length, character, or other form constraint?

quotes:
`module:given_values`. Read a required value: blank or white space only is
missing, anything else kept exactly as written (A02 rules 1, 2).

each with the field it fills: an alias; an object kind; a floor area, a
